reviews.summary: Adding the Would you rather link last round left one sentence holding three clauses joined by 'and ... and', with three links. On a phone it's hard to tell which game does what, and it breaks VOICE.md's short sentences. Splitting it gives each game its own clause.; Same fix in Spanish, so the two versions stay the same post.

'Asks for you' reads as 'requests you' or 'asks after you'. Round 1 fixed the Spanish for the same confusion, but not the English.; The Greater Good instructions have both partners answer every question. 'Take turns on every question' can read as alternating who answers. The Spanish ('contestad los dos cada pregunta por turnos') already says it correctly.; '¿Por qué…?' reads as 'why would you like to be remembered?', not 'what do you want to be remembered for?'. This is the same trap as round 1's 'Por qué se discute'.

Last round's fix was added on to the old answer instead of replacing it, so the same two questions now appear twice in one answer, the snippet Google is most likely to lift for "What are 10 good questions?". The rest of the answer stays as it is.; Same duplication in Spanish: both questions are quoted and then repeated straight after in «Diez buenas para empezar».; Last round's polish was applied as "X, and Y, and Z", a run-on that buries the quiz link. That link is the post's answer to the PAA about couples' quizzes.; Matches the English fix. Removes the "y… y… Y" chain, which reads as translated.
